question: In 2026, for the fourth consecutive year, the municipality of Oradea, Romania, sought to prevent the Pride march from taking place. Despite organisers proposing over 100 alternative routes, the authorities refused to authorise the march, invoking, among other grounds, ‘good morals’. The march nevertheless took place peacefully on 25 July 2026.

Following the march, the Bihor gendarmerie imposed 55 fines, totalling RON 61 500, on participants. These events raise concerns regarding freedom of assembly and non-discrimination, which are protected by Articles 12 and 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union.

Meanwhile, according to the municipality, Oradea received approximately EUR 63 million in EU funds in 2025, including under cohesion policy. Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060, which lays down common rules for several EU funds, including the European Regional Development Fund and the Cohesion Fund, requires respect for fundamental rights and compliance with the Charter in implementing these funds. 1.
How does the Commission assess the compatibility of these restrictions and sanctions with Articles 12 and 21 of the Charter?
Has it assessed whether cohesion programmes benefiting Oradea comply with Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 and the enabling condition concerning the Charter?
If not, will it carry out such an assessment and, where shortcomings are established, what measures will it take?
